# PowerShell Guidelines

## Purpose
Rules for writing and reviewing PowerShell scripts and modules. Target: **PowerShell 7.6 LTS** (`pwsh`, built on .NET 10), cross-platform (Windows, Linux, macOS). Do not write for Windows PowerShell 5.1 (`powershell.exe`) unless the file header says so explicitly.

## Script header
- Start every script with `#Requires -Version 7.6` (plus `#Requires -Modules` / `-RunAsAdministrator` when needed).
- Then comment-based help (`.SYNOPSIS`, `.DESCRIPTION`, `.PARAMETER`, `.EXAMPLE`, `.OUTPUTS`).
- Then `[CmdletBinding()]` and a `param()` block, followed by:
  ```powershell
  Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
  $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
  ```
- Scripts must run from any working directory: build paths from `$PSScriptRoot` with `Join-Path` (which accepts multiple child paths in 7.6).

## Naming and style
- Functions use approved `Verb-Noun` names (`Get-Verb`), singular nouns, and a module-specific prefix for exported commands.
- `PascalCase` for functions, parameters and public variables; `camelCase` for local variables.
- Use full cmdlet and parameter names in scripts, never aliases (`Get-ChildItem -Path`, not `gci` or `ls`) or positional parameters for anything beyond the first obvious one.
- Four-space indentation, One True Brace Style (opening brace on the same line). Format with PSScriptAnalyzer's formatter settings.
- Use splatting (`@params`) for calls with more than three parameters instead of backtick line continuation.
- Single quotes for literal strings, double quotes only when interpolating. Use here-strings (`@' '@`) for multi-line text.

## Functions and parameters
- Every function is an advanced function with `[CmdletBinding()]` and `[OutputType()]`.
- Type every parameter and validate it: `[Parameter(Mandatory)]`, `[ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]`, `[ValidateSet()]`, `[ValidateRange()]`, `[ValidateScript()]`.
- Use `[switch]` for flags, never `[bool]`. Don't default switches to `$true`.
- Support the pipeline (`ValueFromPipeline`, `ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName`) with `begin`/`process`/`end` blocks where it makes sense.
- Functions that change state use `[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]` and check `$PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess()`, so `-WhatIf` and `-Confirm` work. Add `ConfirmImpact = 'High'` for destructive actions.
- Emit objects, not formatted text: return `[pscustomobject]` or classes; never `Write-Host` or `Format-*` for data. Leave formatting to the caller.
- Use `Write-Verbose`, `Write-Debug`, `Write-Warning`, `Write-Information` for messages; `Write-Host` only for interactive UI.
- Don't pollute the output stream: suppress unwanted output with `$null = ...` (faster than `| Out-Null`).

## Error handling
- `try` / `catch` / `finally` with `-ErrorAction Stop` on calls that may fail; catch specific exception types first.
- Report errors in functions with `$PSCmdlet.ThrowTerminatingError()` or `Write-Error` with an `ErrorRecord`, not plain `throw 'text'` in module code.
- Never use empty `catch {}` blocks or `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` to hide real problems; `Ignore` only for expected, harmless failures with a comment.
- For native commands, `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true` makes non-zero exit codes throw; otherwise check `$LASTEXITCODE` after every native call.

## Performance and modern language
- Collect loop results by assigning the loop (`$items = foreach ($x in $list) { ... }`) or with `[System.Collections.Generic.List[T]]`; never `$array += $item` in loops.
- Filter left: use cmdlet parameters (`-Filter`, `-Include`) before `Where-Object`. Use `.Where()` / `.ForEach()` (or their 7.6 aliases `PSWhere()` / `PSForEach()`) for in-memory collections.
- Use `ForEach-Object -Parallel -ThrottleLimit n` or `Start-ThreadJob` for parallel work instead of `Start-Job`.
- Use the ternary operator (`$a ? $b : $c`), null-coalescing (`??`, `??=`), null-conditional member access (`${obj}?.Property`) and pipeline chain operators (`&&`, `||`) where they improve readability.
- Use `[ordered]@{}` when key order matters; `[pscustomobject]@{}` for output objects.
- Use `ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable` / `ConvertTo-Json -Depth n` explicitly; never rely on the default depth.
- `Invoke-RestMethod` with `-Authentication`, `-Token` and `-StatusCodeVariable`; set `-MaximumRetryCount` and `-RetryIntervalSec` for flaky endpoints.

## Cross-platform
- Use `Join-Path`, `[System.IO.Path]` and `$PSScriptRoot`; never hardcode `\` or `/` separators or drive letters.
- Check the platform with `$IsWindows`, `$IsLinux`, `$IsMacOS`.
- Use `$env:TEMP` only on Windows; use `[System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()` for all platforms.
- Files are UTF-8 without BOM (the PowerShell 7 default); set `-Encoding utf8NoBOM` when writing files explicitly.

## Security
- Never hardcode passwords, tokens or keys. Use `Microsoft.PowerShell.SecretManagement` with a vault, `[PSCredential]` parameters (`Get-Credential`) and `[SecureString]`.
- Never use `Invoke-Expression` or build commands from strings; call commands directly with arguments or splatting.
- Don't use `-Force`, `-SkipCertificateCheck` or `Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` to work around problems.
- Sign scripts for production (`Set-AuthenticodeSignature`) when the environment requires `AllSigned` or `RemoteSigned`.
- Validate all external input (parameters, files, API responses) before using it in paths or commands.

## Modules
- One module per folder: `.psd1` manifest, `.psm1` root module, `Public/` and `Private/` function folders.
- Export explicitly with `FunctionsToExport` in the manifest (no wildcards); set `CompatiblePSEditions = 'Core'` and `PowerShellVersion = '7.6'`.
- Install and publish with `PSResourceGet` (`Install-PSResource`, `Publish-PSResource`), not the old `PowerShellGet` cmdlets.

## Testing and quality
- Lint with PSScriptAnalyzer (`Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -Recurse -Settings PSGallery`) with zero warnings.
- Test with Pester 5 (`Describe` / `Context` / `It`, `BeforeAll`, `Should -Be`, `Mock`); tests in `*.Tests.ps1` next to the code or in `tests/`.
- Test `-WhatIf` behavior for every state-changing function.

## Code review focus
Flag in this order: hardcoded secrets or `Invoke-Expression`, missing `SupportsShouldProcess` on destructive functions, swallowed errors or unchecked `$LASTEXITCODE`, aliases and positional parameters, `+=` in loops, `Write-Host` for data, missing parameter validation, platform-specific paths.
